Patient in the sim and understanding of mistakes, will help by giving hints as to what you can fix on the fly. Debrief is succinct and extremely helpful; will most likely give you tips on your next event without you asking, and pass on general techniques to help improve skills all-around. Walks through the gradesheet with you per item to review and see if you've done anything worthy of 5s before he submits it. Above-average grader.

He was kinda rude in a contacts sim for the landing pattern and if you're flying badly he'll trash you in the debrief. Instruments he was way more chill but I was also way better at flying by then, so he may just have high expectations even for new students.

Very approachable personality and laid back in the brief; doesn't go in depth on topics as much as other instructors do unless you want to. Will start by asking questions that skim the surface; if you get them right, he will slowly take over the brief, walk you through the plan, and let you in on some techniques for success. During the sim he is an excellent coach and pays attention to how closely you abide by FTI numbers and procedures, though he may not catch all your mistakes. Thorough and genuinely helpful debrief complete with in-depth gradesheet commentary. Above-average grader. Adheres closely to CTS; though if you impress him enough overall he won't grade you down for some errors, but will leave advice on the gradesheet. Had him for C3401, he used to only teach instruments. Felt great up until I saw the gradesheet, told me I had a great flight and he was impressed. I'm not sure if I did something wrong during the brief, maybe had him on a bad day, or maybe he entered the grade sheet wrong, but I got 3'd on everything except my actual manuevers, with no comments. I'm not sure how brief/BA/comms etc are 3'd but manuevers can be 4'd? Up until this point I've been 4's down the board with a 5 sprinkled in here and there kinda guy. Overall, counting it as a fluke and would agree with everthing said above. He was great in the sim and brief was chill. I hate it when disgruntled people come on here and bitch,not trying to do that. Just wanted to leave this here for others to beware in case it's not a fluke.

Concur that the above gouge probably caught him on an off day or something. N3101 was a great experience with him. If you're in instruments or nav blocks, stay on your toes cause he'll do something weird to you to keep your brain spinning. But overall a great experience. Great grader and teacher. As always, come prepared and it's gonna be a good time. Hoping I get him again

Wants to teach you things sometimes outside the syllabus but arent graded on these <- Concur. He usually won't ding your grades if you miss stuff he introduces that's outside of the syllabus but will reward the knowledge if you know them.

Probably my favorite sim instructor. Not sure how he was in the brief (I had him for a warmup so we kinda just chatted about whatever) but the man is an awesome teacher. Very nice and easy going. He's big on building sight pictures for contact sims (ie might fail some of the stuff on your PFD to get you to fly outside the cockpit). Would love to have him again. Provides a lot of good feedback that will seriously help you. Also likes to throw traffic in your area without it coming up on TCAS so keep the scan going. Very chill instructor

Literally the chill master of the chill masters. You can't escape his chillness. You will still run the brief but you basically can't do any wrong if you show up prepared. Get him going on P-3s and Southwest and he'll give you 4s and 5s across the board

Had him for multiple instrument sims. Absolute chill monster, will probably walk into your brief with a fat lip of Copenhagen. Flew P3's in the Navy and then Homeland Security. So chill it's insane. Come in knowing your stuff and executing basic FTI shit and you'll earn some 5's. If you're scheduled with him, consider yourself blessed
^Will never catch this guy without a fat lip in. Seriously, this dude is the man. Great instructor, chill as hell. Was so chill he wanted to talk about college football during the sim

Had a so so experience. He was definitely chill in the brief and led it for the most part, and in the sim he was very quiet. This was I3100, and it was my first time doing a VOR final. I punched throught the MDA but 20-40' on the first approach and he legitimately yelled at me and told me I had awful aircraft control because i was 118 knots and not 120 (CTS is 120 +10kts or -0kts on final but he way over reacted in my opinion). I messed up on the NTDT final as well and he did the same thing, yelling "MDA, MDA!" Graded still really nicely but those outbursts took me off guard and really ruined my flow for the sim

doesn't teach well, will micro manage your flight and "coach" constantly which might mess your flow during aero or stalls. strict grader and he'll do most of the talking in the brief. Fair grader though.

Way nicer and a better grader in instruments than contacts. As long as you know what you're talking about and perform pretty well on the sim he'll give you a break if your air work falls apart once or twice or miss an ops check

Thought the brief was thorough but fair. Some of the rumors are true and can be a jerk in the sim and stare at you like a disapproving father. Just got to swallow your pride and try to see what he is trying to emphasize and try to get better. Will bring to your attention things you missed or did incorrectly but in my experience that didn't effect my grade, just my disposition at the time. He can somewhat rattle you just because most of the other instructors don't get as intense as he does. Just know he raises his voice for urgency and not so much anger and wants to make you better. But it is an experience and you will probably have above MIF on everything.

Grumpy old dude that expects professionalism and pure business throughout the entire event - brief to sim to debrief. However - extremely condescending to every single question you ask - even ones that pertain to pure technique not referenced in the FTI. That being said, he does seem? Like he cares about making you a better aviator with him strictly being business. Will crack oddly timed jokes that you can't tell if he's just trying to catch you off guard or genuinely lightening the mood. As long as you don't royally screw up he'll pretty much give you straight 4s. Overall - 5/10 instructor.

Is genuinely happy whenever you perform ops checks. Do them at regular intervals for a 5. *long, soft inhale* "Gooooooooooood Blinkerrrr" // Distinctively slow paced, but exceedingly meticulous. Makes a genuine effort to get to know students, and has a hobby of marking the hometowns of every student he's ever worked with in a massive world atlas. In late block sims he may take over your brief, give you ATIS information and clearance in the briefing spaces for you to write down, saving time. Smiles frequently; very pleasant personality and unparalleled patience in the sim to the point that it is difficult to imagine him being angry. Bright and cheery when responding to ops checks, he really enjoys them. Debrief is moderately short yet distinctly in depth and helpful; he will typically give you the notes he took during the sim, and you might feel compelled to keep them because of how nice he is. Above average grader especially with ops checks. He will notice everything you do wrong and note it in the debrief but not in mean way.

Had him for a contact sim. Not sure about anyone else but I couldn't wait to get away from him. Pretty unprofessional and seemingly does not want to be an instructor (dragged his feet into his brief, whatever was bothering him he made it clear he could not compartmentalize). Fair grader but the remarks on the gradesheet were really unfounded, once you look past the spelling errors. I'd be glad if I didn't have another hop with him.

Said he would bitch slap me b/c I turned the wrong way on a PEL(P) haha. He's actually pretty chill though. Is pretty into Hockey (Chicago Blackhawks), seemed genuinely happy during the debrief when we talked hockey for a few minutes. Also jokingly threatened me with violence when I was off altitude a couple times, overall a good teacher and fair grader.
great instructor. he'll be impressed if you do well on brief. will give great advice at your flying to better your technique. very forgiving and you might get a 5 of your knowledge is great.
Really bridges the gap between natops/ Fti and practical application. ^treats sims as a relaxed learning environment if you know your stuff.

Excellent instructor. Brief is informative and there are no stupid questions. I fumbled my way all the way through I3105 and he said I "made par" as far as I3100 goes, so there's an added nice bonus too. He also probably gave the most valuable advice and info I've received. Asks if you have questions quite a bit, so come prepared with literally anything. If you just ask him how to be a better pilot he'll probably have something for you. Agree with excellent upside down writing skills.

This is as of OCT2021, flew I3203 with him and I can say i did not see the man that some of the gouge underneath says he is. 0650 brief and he came in smiling and happy drinking coffee. Sure we talked discuss items, got a little farther in depth than normal, but even if I wasn't totally sure of something, he was still happy to explain what he was talking about. Sim went fine, we tried some things that i hadn't seen before and i felt i got some good experience and knowledge out of it. Debrief was fine, pretty fair grades. He did several less than obvious malfunctions with the A/C so maintain SA/good ops checks/scan. Overall, the experience was a positive stressful experience. It was stressful for the sake of learning and self-improvement, not because he was out to get me. Happy with the experience and outcome. Guy that said "gg" below sounds like he didn't know what he was doing and so he had a bad sim but blames Major Torres. Classic.

Okay this guy was actually great. He briefs HARD expect him to ask you challenging questions but if you handle them well as in answer them correctly, or logically give your best answer or humbly say you dont know he will respect you. He genuinly wanted me to succeed. He asked me a random EP so have those down. During the sim he wasnt super hands on but instead gave advice here and there. He graded fairly and definitely gave me a better grade than I deserved in one Block. Afterwards he gave me honest advice from his own career about studying and working hard. I loved this man.

Maybe it was a bad morning to be Techno, but wasn't personable at all during our instrument event. Below miffed me twice because I made two mistakes on my jet log/DD175, and didn't have the route loaded properly in the FMS. Wouldn't say he was an asshole necessarily, but corrects your mistakes almost backhandedly. Couldn't wait to get away from him.

Brief was overall smooth for I2103. Asked a few questions. Doesn't show a whole lot of emotions so you might question how you are doing throughout the whole event. Not overbearing in the sim. Make sure to include an opps check and climb/descent checklist if applicable. Sticks close to CTS on manuevers and will let you know when you are deviating too far. Fair grader, will give you over MIF for 80% of the items.

During I3205 he decided to fail my comms and make me do the whole instrument flight with no FMS and only 1-way radio coms. The whole brief was about ADSBs and digital vs analog communication. Was reading the FIH in flight and was overall not having a good time in the sim. He graded me decently and even said "i know i kind of beat you up in the sim but hopefully you are better prepared." I guess I am but I probably missed a few 5s that I could have gotten had I done the event as it was intended to be done.

New instructor from the FITU. Expect to run through the whole brief and all discuss items. He loves to quote specifics from the FTI so be prepared to talk specifically about things straight from the FTI. Doesn't say too much in the plane. Will let you mess up hoping that you correct it. Don't be afriad to talk through your thought process on point to point, etc. He was a really nice grader giving lots of 4 and some 5s on things I did well. You'll be chilling if you fly with him

He's with CNATRA.Very laid back and fairly quiet in the brief and flight, forgiving of simple mistakes and helps you learn from them without making you feel like an idiot. I got assigned to brief with him earlier than when my standby was supposed to be, so I was feeling less prepared than I would have liked but it turned out to be a great flight. 10/10 would fly with him again.

Nice guy, pretty relaxed in the brief (cut my hydraulics system explanation short and just had me skip to the next topic). Can be a nit picky on some things (ie wants you to point out and explain each part while doing the exterior inspection), but overall very nice and helpful in the brief and plane. Grades very fairly, but he expects you to know your stuff.
Very quiet and laid back in the brief and in the plane. Overall had a great time flying with him. Loves to talk about the C130!
Goofy guy. Super friendly. Knows his stuff though and expects you to as well. Great teacher in the plane and thorough in the debrief.

Brief: Standard NATOPS, he ended up briefing me on discussion items even though I came prepared. Asked maybe a few questions. He recommended Griffs Gouge on Youtube for instrument flying. He handled most coms in the plane and was super fun to fly with. One of my favorite flights of primary so far. Highly recommend.

Very laid back in the brief, will let you figure it out if you make a mistake instead of jumping your ass. In the plane he's pretty quiet but will give good demos if you're struggling. During the debrief he doesn't give exact feedback comparative to your gradesheet so I would wait on your grades before making assumptions about the flight. Overall a chiller and good to fly with.
Also a very experienced T-6 Pilot, he instructed NFO's in Pensacola flying the T-6A. He's a very good IP to ask questions about the aircraft and techniques on how to do things well.

Really into EPs, Limits, and NWC in briefs. Get out of the brief, and he's chill in the airplane. He is a good teacher and genuinely cares about your success. His tips in the airplane are helpful. Debriefs are good and he tells you where to improve. Won't officially say but will challenge you to a staring contest while you are briefing.
In my experience, super relaxed and asks the important questions. He's not there to expose any unimportant knowledge, very practical and honest in his feedback.
Good instructor with relevant feedback. Super chill in brief and in the plane.
New STUCON O, Very good IP, interested in knowing about you. Really works to make sure you succeed.

Tries to be as hands off as possible and will let you mess up to an extent. He will give you positive reinforcement and is a good teacher. I left feeling more confident, however, he does not grade very generously

In the brief, he was chill but very much about getting it done as soon as possible. Not sure if it was just my day, but we did the discussion items after the flight. As you're going to the airplane, he quizzes you on the preflight. Nothing out of left field. In the airplane, very chill. I didn't feel him aiding the controls at all. He might sound stern in the airplane when he's telling you something to look out for; however, he is also quick to give you a compliment when you've done something well. If he sounds stern, don't let it get to you because it's just a comment. It'll literally pass in seconds. Fair grader overall. The debrief was helpful.

Flew with him on a weekend so take this with a grain of salt. He's a reservist so expect to fly even if weather looks a little weird. Took a bunch of time in the brief to look over weather since we had a bunch of bad weather coming in. We were able to stay legal although we had to change of flight plans. Briefing was pretty easy, standard brief. Be prepared to talk about every point in the brief and you'll be good to go. For instruments we did a Tango 3 and stayed local. He took controls and let me setup for my approaches for almost every approach which made things a bit easier. Standard instrument flight
Is a newer IP and is great for instruments. Call sign is "Radio" so make sure to get those coms down.
Quick and to the point in the brief, doesn't like to waste time. Really fun to fly with, super patient in the plane and it a great teacher. Watch out for a beer fine over something really small.

Onwing - Genuinely cares and wants you to learn the most out of the flight. Iron the brief out and you'll jump right into the plane asap. Semi concur on the beer fine, he hates the easily fixed mistakes ie: not setting CDI or resetting bugs. Don't let the small stuff slip because you feel youre doing well overall and you'll have a great flight

Stoic in the while your briefing, initially comes across serious. Overall, super willing to teach and is a great instructor. Thorough in the debrief. Will ask a lot of questions in the brief and gets excited when you know the answers, definitely a positive reinforcement kinda guy.

Chill instructor, asked questions about the NWCs. Very helpful in the air and is willing to teach. Took an hour to debrief because he wanted to go through everything in a lot of detail which I appreciated

NATOPS Wiz. Big on checklists and wants FWB and applicable NOTAMs printed for the brief. At least for early events wants to teach and will do so during the brief. During FAM check will fail MFDs and is big on exterior inspection. Have a paper/notebook for the debrief.

P-8 guy. Loves instrument events. Among the quickest briefs I've ever had for a flight, in instruments expect standard NATOPS, and glancing at the discuss items, won't correct you but will add on if he thinks there is something important that you missed. Very communicative in the plane, and very reassuring. Very helpful on teaching techniques for instruments.

Endure. Speaking for the FAM side especially early on if you come knowing your stuff in the brief you will have a good time, She doesnt shake hands for some reason idk. Biggest tip is good attitude and be respectful, sounds crazy but I pity the fool that gives her any lip. In the plane its rough because she is heavy on the controls. Unholy amounts of control pressure from her.

Feels like she doesnt trust me to fly the plane straight and level. Doesnt help she is a ground school instructor. Knows the 3710 like the back of her hand and will not let you leave the debrief until you also know it. Also, never IMSAFE out of a flight or sim just because of gouge. Nobody became a great pilot without experiencing all ends of the spectrum. The point is for you to learn and she will ensure that you do. Suffer the pain of discipline AND regret.

She grades fairly but kinda treats you like a kid. Generally thinks you're more overwhelmed than you are. She's a really nice person and I think a Tactical IMSAFE is a little extra... Cares about teaching and fixing your weak spots. She's very approachable and if you have any questions or irks she's really accomodating. Come prepared for the brief

I flew an event with him, plan was changed to a Tango-3 due to bad weather, the flight itself didn't seem too bad and the debrief wasn't too bad either, however I was hammered on the gradesheet. I asked another student who had him for I41XX block too and also agreed that he grades super rough for I41XX block events. Admittedly Tango-3's are tough especially for a early inexperienced instrument student, however I do think my grades were lower than other IP's would've given. (Update flew with him again, grades were far better the next time, but went on a more standard instrument profile and was able to perform better.)
Relatively relaxed in the brief, but can become a demon in the plane. Genuinely a good dude though and teacher when he's out of the plane.
Offwing - Super relaxed in the brief. Pretty laid back in the plane as well. Super fun to fly with and gives great advice during the debrief.

He was super nice in the plane and really took time to teach things especially in the pattern. It was a bad hop overall personally and he hit me pretty hard on grades even though he said I was on pace during my 4202 flight. Overall most of that was on me and he was chill.
TACTICAL IMSAFE / CHILL UNTIL NOT

Knows the CNAF and Natops extensively so just keep that in mind. Chill in the Brief, will ask you what coaching style works best for you and will apply that in the airplane. Chill in the airplane and debrief. His debriefs are in-depth and helpful. Just get ouf of the brief and have a good event.
Genuinely helpful and likes discussing things in depth. Enjoys answering hypothetical questions. Very willing to help out in the plane as well.
Asks a lot of questions in the brief and drives most of the brief. Is super fun to fly with a good instructor and will give you a good confidence boost.
Concur. Has some great USMC experience and will extend the debrief to help you think about your career. Loved to fly with him. He nerds out about fuel management and would love if you did too.

Know your stuff in the brief, really helps for the rest of the flight. Sometimes wants to get into the weeds with discussion but it's not with a "gotcha mindset" she genuinely wants you to understand and prepare you for future flights.

Absolutely can confirm on the getting prepped for future flights, I had her for a warmup after I was out of the plane for a bit and I was just not myself. Did a lot of things wrong, but she asked questions that are the exact format you'd get on a checkride and I wasn't able to answer them easily (FAM42XX Block) and I have modified my study regime and how I think about certain things like the ADB and Preflight

He knows FTI, Natops, SOP, etc… inside and out, but understands we won't be on his level of knowledge. He asks a lot of questions, and would rather you say "I don't know" than try and guess. Overall flying with him will be a great experience.

Maybe its cause he's my onwing but I feel he really cares about you learning to fly and understanding things rather than trying to get you into the weeds of discussion items. Tends to take controls a good amount, even when I felt it wasn't really needed but otherwise, fun to fly with and a great guy overrall.
Not his onwing and can confirm, very chill. Really cares about teaching and helping you improve.

Hilarious in the brief, will make jokes, has a lot of T-6 hours so he trusts you alot with the plane and will give you a longer leash because he knows his limits with the aircraft. His debriefs are long, and if it looks like a weather cancel and he doesn't have another flight after he will sit you down and encourage you to ask questions about primary, i.e. what's expected of you and what he would focus on knowing if he was you.

Brief: You'll brief in his office, not at the whiteboard, so bring a printout. He'll stare at you the whole time - don't let it throw you. He might widen his eyes mid-brief just to see if it messes with you. Stick to your plan and practice try to stare back and don't get rattled. For QODs, go deeper than just filling in the blank - he'll probably ask follow-ups about systems from NATOPS. In the plane: Super chill in the T6 and a great instructor. Doesn't do the whole "helmet fire" thing. He won't overload you, but be solid on comms and respond quickly when things are directed at you, absolutely don't cue your mic and go "ummmm". Debrief: Very thorough and detailed. Only downside is there's so much feedback you'll need to prioritize/triage what to fix first. Honestly though, it's a good problem to have. You'll know exactly what can be improved upon for next time. Grades fairly as well, there is not a single grade I recieved from him so far that I thought wasn't 100% correct. If your scheduled for a COPC: Should be the same vibe. If you get him, don't stress - just prep well using what's here and go crush it. He went through one himself when he was here.

Flies for Southwest. Priorities are "have fun, be safe, learn something." Great with answering questions in the plane and will help you out if you ask. A little quiet and has a bit of a rbf but is a good IP to fly with.
Says fuck a lot like it's a sentence enhancer. Beer is Coors Banquet, the tan can. Very pointedly went down and MIF'd every item.
New IP. Funny guy, lot of energy, super helpful. Very very stingy giving any 5s but reluctant to give 3s too

Great flight with him for FAM42XX block, we flexed a ton to get all the things done we needed to during the flight and went outside the normal boundaries of contacts flights due to WX and massive traffic volume in the area. Ended up earning a 5 on Mission Planning/Execution due to being able to flex so much and stay cool the whole time.

Really cool to fly with, also super knowledgeable about the plane. Very good instructor. I learned a ton when flying with him and is fun to brief with. Played the rolling stones out of his phone when walking to the plane.
Flying with him is great. Brief… know your NWC's as well as knowing the system you're briefing inside and out.
Have your NWCs down, will stare at you and wait. Doesn't matter if your EP has 11 of them. Have them all. Fine in the flight. Grades the flight fairly.

Know your procedures and NWC (Not verbim). He will give you time to rember these if you are struggling, but he seriously will unsat you if dont know the procedures and MOST of the NWC. If you make it to the plane, he is amazing to fly with, a great teacher, and honest grader.

In my experience if you show you know what you're talking about he will talk more in discussions then you. Don't be afraid to ask questions. Will let you know if you're wrong and not in a condescending way. Has a give a fuck factor.
Is a super new IP. She is very nice in the brief, come prepared and she doesn't ask a lot of questions. Is pretty quiet in the plane, she wants to see you succeed. "Fly good, don't be dumb"
Very chill on XC and great to fly with. Hands off (unless you need help), just ask. Will let you mess stuff up and fix it. Know your knowledge for the brief and you will have a great lesson.
Can confirm polar bear chill
Very patient in the plane, good teacher. Is a new IP. A little hard to talk to, but overall is a very nice person and understanding. SUPER LONG DEBRIEF

Good owning instructor. Know your ADB, exterior inspection, NWC's. Is patient, however just know your stuff and you'll do fine. Debrief takes a long time, but you get to know what to work on for the next flight.
Super nice and fun to fly with, adheres hard to cts and doesn't grade too generously, however won't below mif even if you mess up
I have been below-MIF'd by him for relatively minor things (e.g. one missed ATC call) but otherwise concur
Very nice guy, looking to teach and not give you a ton of shit.

Brief was super laid back. He did have me brief wearing all of my flight gear so just a heads up. If there's anything you want to work in particular, let him know and you'll tailor your flight accordingly. In the airplane, really chill gives usefull advice/tips/coaching. I'm pretty sure he said "meow, meow,meow" during GXs. Debrief was helpful, he has 2000 hours in the T-6 and did the Checkride for Maj Kuchinin. He has a dry sense of humor and is sarcastic, so just keep that in mind with his comments in the airplane/debrief. He means no malice.
Brief: Did not care at all. Told me to skip my NATOPs brief and we just glanced at weather. Mildly briefed. Fun and chill in plane and helpful. Epic reservist.

Not sure if it was because it was an aero flight but overall very fun flight and good teacher. Show up with good knowledge of procedures and discuss items. He really likes fast ground ops, so the quicker you are the better and I think it sets a great tone for the rest of the flight.
Haven't flown with him but this doesn't at all match what others say about him.

most people meet him it's their worst days of primary, and he is the grim reaper when it comes to that. however, he is an intelligent guy and gets a lot of students grief for it (he unsatted me once in contacts)

Reservist, pretty quick in the brief, prioritizes getting to the aircraft. Asks some questions during the exterior inspection. Does a lot of good coaching while flying. Grades well and overall an insightful and pretty chill flight.

Awesome in the airplane, hardly touches the controls at all unless to demo. In the brief, very relaxed, but wants to make sure you know the material/flight profile. Very thorough and helpful with the debrief. Honest grader. Overall, incredibly chill, show up knowing what you need to know and have a good event.

Former Navy Helo guy, also Navy Helo and T-34 instructor. Very nice, asked a few personal questions; seems genuinely interested in getting to know you. Had him for I2102 - had me brief maneuvers step by step and also brief the maneuvers for the next sim event so be sure to be looking ahead/ familiar. Good overall instructor, provides lots of tips and techniques for going forward. Tough grader.
I3101. Not easy instructor by any means. Not huge on talking a lot while doing comms. Wants very st and to the point comms. For example I said ".....level 5000 with information Bravo, request…" and
she said its needs to be "...5000, bravo, request…" aside from that she does grade better than you would think.
Make sure you have a few questions going into the brief. If you don't she takes that as you know everything. This annoys her, and she will be a little hard on you.
I heard she's "one of the four semen" after I already had her, and I get the joke, but don't get yourself all worked up about it. She's not generous, but not +

unfair. She'll throw you some curveballs, so make sure you know what you're checking when you go through checklists. Definitely be well prepared for the brief, because she will make sure you know your stuff.

Loves to say "devil is in the details", and will live up to it. For example, no one tells you, and usually your instructor will just tell you in the brief, that I2101-I2104 are all done with an NSE1 clearance, not an NSE2 (if you look in the briefing guide, it just says IFR instead of VFR, and you're supposed to figure out that its NSE1). I called for clearance with NSE2 and she just told me no. I also called tower for takeoff and said everything right except "...ready for takeoff" instead of "...ready for departure". I also said "cutting power" instead of "reducing power" on a maneuver. All of these in things she just said "No." and kind of waited and watched me flounder around and try to guess what I said wrong. Not that it wasn't my fault, but she seemed re keen than others on setting off helmet fires and watching you try to figure it out.

Day nav sim- If you catch her on one of her "off days", just IMSAFE out of it. Literally the st unpleasant experience I've had in primary so far, and I came extremely well prepared. She kept telling me how since the time she came through flight school, the quality of aviator is about 30% worse, whatever that means, and that "students suck at reading charts and at comms". Also proceeded to berate me in the sim when I said "with information Charlie" instead of "Charlie". Oh, and told me that there's no way I'd be flying anything but helicopters. All in all, having a sim with her was an extremely deralizing experience, enough for me to take the time to write a paragraph about it.

Very good at getting in your head from the beginning and gives looks that make you second and triple guess yourself. FOLLOW NATOPS TO THE T for EPs, don't do technique-ish stuff because as she told me we are just learning to fly, so leave the fancy fluff out and follow the NATOPS. Have stuff merized verbatim, and will just say no when you aren't right and wait for you to figure it out. Definitely got in my head a bit and created some helmet fire. However, the debrief was great, her teaching style is rough in the ment but afterwards you really learn how much stuff you don't actually know/don't have merized well enough. Her lessons are definitely eye opening to your personal stcomings.
Know the NATOPS statement on sound judgment verbatim for I2104

I3203: She's a ball-buster. Be humble or she will humble you. And by humble I mean have questions to start the brief like one of the other comments mentions. She said she used to be the wing stan OIC for the instrument phase of training. So she is way re picky about stuff like comms than other instructors. Don't let her get in your head with mistakes.

I2101. I went into the brief with 5 or 6 questions that I picked out so it would be apparent that I had studied and read the fti. I also made sure to talk about errors I already experienced when I was practicing the day before. She was super excited that I asked what I did and we had a conversation about it. In the sim she was a good teacher. I understand how she may rub you the wrong way with how she "corrects" deviation from airspeed, altitude, etc… For example, I was 90 feet low and she said altitude three times then said "it took three alternatively itude warnings before I saw a positive rate of climb." Also, the statement above is true wrt the NSE1 vs. NSE2. She got a little frustrated when i made the same mistake
C2102 - Pulled the fire emergency when I was shutting down the engine at the end.

I2101- talks to you while in a turn so stay focused on rollout heading and have tough skin. Also listen when she says turn 360* or turn 180*, got upset and didn't answer me when I asked what she wanted me to roll out on a second time. Fair grader though.

C2103: I came as prepared as possible and she still found every single fault in me. I kept a positive attitude and a smile on my face and I think that made a big difference. Come prepared to have your balls busted and for her to try and make you feel like you suck. She had me flying out to the A and making calls to Jax ctr. And approach, which was odd since the whole sim was about abort takeoff procedures. Told me at the debrief my performance would be unsat terrority in later sims, but then said overall really nice job. So not really sure where I stood with her.
Super nice dude who works with you to methodically think things through
Aero sim liked to take the stick from me

Had him for C2102, super nice and provided lots of helpful hints. Very much a technique driven guy. There was very little chit chat in the brief or in the sim. If i made a mistake he didnt freak out he just provided me with some feedback and we kept rolling along

Also had for C2102. Soft spoken, very helpful. Asked some systems knowledge, answered any question I had by getting me to walk myself through to the answer. Agree that he is patient and provides a lot of feedback. Didn't really ask any brief related questions.
C2101: Soft spoken Coast Guard helo guy. Super nice and did the entire brief. Good grader if your checklists are down.
Great instructor helped me with things I told him I was weak on and really helped me understand BIs.

I2104: One of my best experiences yet. After doing well on the BI material, he was very interested in helping me prepare for the landing pattern SIM to come very soon, and tried searching for an OFT to run me through it. Couldn't find one, so he sat and talked me through it for another 20-30 minutes. Dude actually cares for you to learn something. Graded me well.

I had back to back instrument sims. Hes cool. He'll take up the entire brief time so be prepared to brief everything on the briefing guide. But as long as you're prepared it'll be fine and even if you don't know a thing here and there, he'll go over it with you. Grades pretty nicely in my opinion and I'd say the sim actually goes pretty well unless you absolutely get lost in the sauce.

Had him for I2201 and I3101. Be overly prepared for your brief, he goes pretty in depth. I would recommend looking at your next event and knowing how to do the next procedure. For both of these sims we practiced the next sim's maneuvers and I wasn't really prepared, but he didn't hold it against me. It would be good practice if you had an idea of what your were doing. Grades nicely.

He was chill. Only did one ep on C2103. Likes if you offer to lead the brief and likes to talk with you all throughout the sim. Depending on your event though, he could expect re or less from you if you are further ahead
C3201. Great guy. Ask questions and he'll answer them better than you could hope; very knowledgeable. Really easy to work with.
Super cool dude and if you're in VT2 hope you get to fly a check ride with him. He'll talk the whole flight and take a couple landings giving you a break.

Excellent instructor. I had him for my first SIM and he was super nice, very helpful, and gave great insight for not only doing well in the SIM but also later down the road flying here. Have a solid grip on your briefing material so that he will see you put in the work and in return will make the SIM fun and enjoyable.

FAM2202: Very nice and friendly. He will test your knowledge (nothing crazy) a bit during the brief so be prepared. Had a few questions prior to starting the sim and was happy to answer and draw out things on his ipad so that I would get a better understanding. During the sim itself, he would pause and we'd discuss anything that I was having a problem with and then reattempt until I felt comfortable enough with it. Post sim gave me a deep breakdown of everything I did well and what I didn't do well with good constructive criticism and not just telling me the things I sucked at. Overall a very good instructor for teaching.

He's the youngest instructor here. Had him for C3203. Kind of an oddball, but not necessarily in a bad way. Be prepared for a very different sim environment than you're used to. He likes jokes and having fun, and part of that is throwing some crazy stuff at you. Be ready for an emergency right after takeoff at KNSE requiring a PEL/P. If you prefer a very professional cockpit environment, do you g r best to roll with his style and even if he gets off track, just keep following your script. For crosswinds, we threw a full 25 kts at me with lightning and blowing debris on the ground. Just focus on flying the pattern and you'll be fine. Also, he's big on ground references during the pattern. Evergreen is his favorite OLF. Overall, I enjoyed having a sim with him even if it was an unusual one. Plus, I learned from it.
^ 25 knots? That's cute. Gave me a 60 knot X-wind and then a 120 headwind. I landed the T-6 like a Harrier, flew backwards, and had a blast.
^120 knots? That's cute. I flew through a tornado that eventually caught on fire. Landed like a meteor, got recruited by the space force.
^tornado? That's cute. I flew through billions and billions and billions and billions of knots
Ask him about the letter of commendation he keeps in "break glass in case of emergency container" it's a good story.
was pretty pissed as he made me go through the entire checklist on C2101. Bullshit
absolute hammer. Had him for C2102 and C2201. Dont give him lists like the FTI, just going to have to sit there and take it. Learned a lot but pretty aggressive over the mic

Saw the above comments and went into the brief dreading the event a bit. However, he's a super cool instructor. Tests your knowledge on the procedures during the brief, but you should already know that. Enjoyed doing the instrument hop with him.

Can be picky about certain things. May start pulling circuit breakers during checklists so your TAD isn't working or simulate the chip light as soon as you turn on the battery (so you might silence the master warning and just look at the amps and totally miss the Chip light). But overall a really good guy; will teach you a thing or two

Definitely picky but super nice dude. Know every single thing you are checking for when you do the hollywood checklist. He will quiz you on a lot of stuff and throw a lot at you but he isn't a dick about it.
Likes to sketch out systems, point to different parts, and ask you about them while explaining why something happens/why a certain EP is necessary.

A great instructor. Picky about being consistent with the hollywood script, but in a constructive way. Very patient. For C2102, he wants to know numbers for the briefing items, and the reasons listed in NATOPS. In the actual sim, he goes crazy with the circuit breakers. Make sure that when you are doing your scan for engine start that you are actually looking at the gauges and registering if they are ving properly. Over all, great instructor!

I2103 - He really hammers you on trim. Constantly told me to take my hands completely off the controls so we could both evaluate how well had it trimmed, even during maneuvers. Had me do half of the timed turn without my hands on the controls, just letting the trim hold it in place. Pretty loose with maneuvers; he completely walked away from the sim two or three times while I was in the middle of a graded maneuver and only returned after I finished it. Overall, he's super helpful for basic airwork and spends most of his time trying to coach you to get better. He's a fair grader, just be prepared to get your balls busted.

Confirming that he loves to mess with circuit breakers. Had him for C2202 and he tested me on most of the abnormal starts and had me do emergency ground egress again so make sure you stay familiar with the indicators. Brief was pretty tough as he went really in depth with the oil, fuel, and hydraulic systems. Know the numbers, locations, and components of any system that might be related to one of the EP's you'll be tested on. Very nice but don't let it lull you into complacency.
C3101 turns off PFD and BFI to get you "looking outside" and then gives 3s for maneuvers. Brief was straight forward.

C2202: Favorite instructor so far. Yes he pops breakers (and he knows this gouge about himself, zero f*cks given), but he does it as a teaching point. He's not going to dock you for not realizing it's an breaker at first, he prefers you go through the recognition process and then come to the conclusion about the breaker. Taught me a ton. Yes his brief was mostly about systems, be able to break down the major engine components. Gives good advice for your next sim.
C2102 - Definitely comes across tough/intimidating in the brief. He asked me numbers for things I didn't think I was required to know, but I don't think it made a difference in my grades.
Can confirm he likes to pop circuit breakers, but it makes for a fun learning experience if you relax and diagnose the situation. Overall, really enjoyed having him as an instructor. Learned alot.
Very loud and enthusiastic, expects you to be on point but willing to help you if you ask questions
Very loud and expects a lot. He is the first sim instructor that I felt made me better though. Make sure you know your stuff and he isn't to bad.

I2104. He is very demanding in the brief. This sim didn't really have that much new material, but he made me describe what the BFI has on it and all the differences from the PFD. He was not satisfied until I literally said everything there was to say about the BFI. He is a good instructor once you get in the sim, demanding but is willing to coach. You can't do enough ops checks, do one every 10-15 min.
Not sure why he gets such a bad rep...very knowledgeable and helpful. He's loud but doesn't yell

Gonna emphasize again to do the OPs checks for him. He tallies how many you do and if you hit 5 you're golden. He says just to be safe to do them before starting any maneuver because then you'll be sure to have as enough. May have been a fluke but I was one OPs check st at the end so I did two basically subsequently and he still counted both towards my tally…
Has the Navy's record for st hours in a T-34

Great instructor. Very particular about ops checks as stated above, but does a great debrief and is fun to fly with in the sim. HUGE Gator fan, easy to get onto a tangent about UF or college football. Preps you ahead for the next event in the debrief. Fair grader.

Fantastic instructor. He will be loud and coach A LOT during the sim. Multiple sim freezes and even demo'd the pattern with crosswinds inside the sim. You will have the largest "helmet fire" of your life. However, if you power through, he will help you improve and learn a lot by the end of the event. Best advice would be to not shut down during the coaching and have a receptive attitude. Be enthusiastic and coachable, and you will see huge progress. Takes his time to give you a real debrief unlike some instructors and actually gives tips. Fair grader.
I2102 - nice guy definitely wants to teach you so come with questions. Not a super hard ass. From Minnesota likes the Vikings a lot and flew Sierras in the Navy.

I2103 - new guy has been working here 2 months as of July 2025. Wife is a nurse, he went to the Naval Academy. Very willing to answer questions about anything you have about primary. Definitely a teacher and not a grader which is always nice. Straight forward sim went through all the graded items. 10/10
FAM2201 - Amazing instructor. Loves NFL football and talking about airplanes. Show up prepared, know why you do the procedures, and he'll be more than happy to teach you.
Super chill guy, really breaks everything down and talks to you like an actual human being
Great instructor, asks a lot of questions in the brief but they were all fair questions from the briefing guide. For the flight he is very positive and he definitely made me better at PELs.
Laid back and very helpful. Provided good criticism and encouragement throughout the sim

Very nice guy and fair grader. You will learn a lot from him. Had him for C2101. Know the fine print of the hollywood checklist because he will ask you what you are looking for during certain steps of the procedures. For me he threw on a fuel balance caution on the EICAS while on the ground, know that you can toggle the fuel balance switch to man/reset to eliminate that warning. Also check the altimeters after you set them because he had me get updated altimeter settings from ground.

Fam3102 - great instructor, helped a lot with the landing pattern during the sim. Will have you fly with the HUD to start and then have you fly mostly off of sight picture as a teaching lesson/outside reference for the actual plane. Will discuss the entire pattern and positions/power settings during brief so have a good understanding of that. Asked about ABCDONT. Did landings at evergreen rw 01 North

Funny and enthusiastic instructor, but very loud and pushy in the sims. Does a lot of coaching, but has great techniques. Some are obscure to understand in accordance with what you have likely been studying (FTI, etc.), but they do work. Be prepared for a bit of helmet fire, but he'll put in a lot of effort toward teaching you
Very intense but amazing instructor. Really wants you to learn without making you feel like you don't know anything.

I had him for C3101 and I'm a big fan. He can tell if you're not totally prepared he's willing to help you through it with some of the numbers you don't remember, but if you seem like you know your stuff he'll let you run with it. He can be kind of quiet during the actual sim, letting you sort of do your thing as long as you're doing well, and kept asking me what I wanted to do next. If you start by catching your own checklists (Ops check, climb, PSA) and clearing turns he'll start telling you not to worry about it. All round very cool guy, HUGE college football fan, and clearly there to make you better. Told me in the brief he was hoping to get some practice breaks at the end, wound up getting a couple and even getting one on the ground.
Favorite instructor by far.

Fam6203 - good instructor was a AF pilot. Chill guy but has his way of doing things that he will teach. Talked about using RW length to gauge distance for initial call's at OLF and some more terrain feature stuff for outbound course rules. We did RW 28 @ evergreen and 5 lakes CR back to RW 32
A rare fan of both Alabama and Auburn

C2103: Definitely did not have the experience stated above. I believe he was training a new instructor, Nick (fmr Marine C-130, not sure on last name), and I don't know if he was trying to prove himself, but he docked me on the brief for not knowing a particular in the weeds number after I thought I was killing it with Nick. Maybe he was trying to get in my head or something but he gave me a 3 for the brief for literally not knowing one number. Then I got 4s and 5s on the sim. So I don't know what to tell you. Maybe he was having a bad day and this is an anomaly, but I hope to never have him again.

Gives way too many techniques that probably st definitely should not be done when you get into the airplane for the first time or your on-wing will be scared/confused/angry. Not a great instructor, at least for warthomatanm-up sims.

Not particularly nice, nor funny. Straight forward guy. We had a 5 minute brief, basically said we'll see what you know when we get to the sim. *During OPS check he messed with cockpit alt. Not much of a debrief, told me he did better and worked harder and he had 4 kids when he was in flight school. Surprisingly nice grader / comments - compared to his criticality in other aspects.
Fair grader. Just want you to be accurate. Straight and to the point. Know your procedures and everything is good.

Continually messed with my systems, popping CBs for flaps, pressurization etc., to check if I was actually looking where I should be. Constantly felt like I was barely keeping up but he graded me well. Don't expect any fives out of him though.

C3101-After reading the above briefs I was nervous going into my sim with him but he's actually one of the st helpful instructors that I've had so far. If you go into the brief super prepared and show you put effort into it and have questions to ask then he's very nice. He'll be very picky with what you say if it isn't perfect, but not in a mean way-just making sure you have it right. Fair grader but the above reviews are right in that he doesn't just hand out 5s

Had him for 2200 instrument sim and he was cool. Didn't try to trip me up, just gave helpful tips and chatted throughout. Goes without saying that you have to know your stuff, I'm sure if you fumble he'll be annoyed
Had him as ground school instructor. Very knowledgeable and did add some hur to the class. He was good about giving you the information that you needed.
One of the best instructors I've had so far, know your procedures in detail and he is re of a coach than a proctor in the sim. I2102

C2101 great instructor. If you know your checklists and radio calls well he will prep you for the upcoming sims i.e. maneuvers, course rules. It is true he will mess with stuff while you are doing checks such as an ops check just pay attention and you will catch it. He gave me props for catching high cockpit altitude on my ops check and oil temp fail during the before landing checklist.

I3103- 10/10 would not recommend. Prebrief lasted around 45 min and dived in really deep into the EP, all the warnings cautions etc… Altered a lot of the briefed flight plan so nothing that was studied for was useful.
I2202- Very helpful and informative. Will correct you if you are off but not in a manner meant to stress you out. Would def recommend!
I don't know if I just didn't vibe with the guy, but I felt he came off very rude during event - - graded fairly but least favorite sim have had, maybe I've just had really great previous instructors

Fam3103 - Good instructor, cool southern dude that flew helos in the navy. Rips 8mg zyns. Will be a good sim if you show up knowing the briefing guide. Had me do crosswing landings at Brewton rw 06. If you're doing okay with pretty tame winds he will start to throw some wild stuff at you just for fun and to give you the experience. Kind of a quiet guy so come with questions and he will give you the info/help you need. 9.1/10

This dude is pretty cool. Seems like a grumpy old dude but that's just his personality. If you come in and know the procedures and briefing items cold you'll have no problem. He wants to teach you, not hold your hand so if you aren't prepared, he could get pretty angry. If you know your stuff, he is super helpful and lets you try different things outside the procedures to see why we do things the way we do.
Grumpy old man who was too aggressive grabbing the stick if you didn't perform exactly how he wanted.

C3203: He was really great in the brief explaining his expectations for the sim, asked a few questions in the brief, but really didn't expect too much (maybe because it was End of Block). Allowed me to make mistakes in the PELs so I could see how they would work out, and if I could recover from on them. We finished quickly, so he just started adding in crazy crosswinds in various directions to prepare me for the next sim.
C2201 show up with a solid understanding of the EPs and CAMIs cold and he roywill only throw a few at you and shoot the breeze the rest of the time. Awesome instructor.
C2101: awesome person, he ran through the whole brief and explained things clearly. Walked me through on flying in the sim all the way to the ground even though it was fam 1.

I2101: great sim, he takes a while on the brief for this one to talk to you about why instruments matter. He teaches you a lot and he has a vast aunt of experience to back it up. Great instructor in the sim, guided me through the steep turns and timed turns. Expects you to never accept being off, so constantly make adjustments to fix your airspeed/altitude/heading and you will be all set. He has a positive and reinforcing attitude
I2201. Dude looks like Larry King and is (justifiably) salty. May seem cold and curt but isn't too bad in the sim. Grades well if you know your stuff. Prior A4 dude who has ejected twice apparently.
Had him for my second sim. He scribbled all over the briefing sheet as I talked and asked questions in very peculiar ways. Grades harder than st in my opinion.

I3101/I3205: Legitimately the worst instructor I've ever had. Just condescending and not helpful at all. Everything turns into an argument with him. Not sure he really wants to be there. I'd have thought I failed the I3205 with the way he acted. Told me my numbers were wrong for the Jet Log and i responded "This is what I calculated, I don't go off of the one on the briefing guide because there is wrong info on them." And basically told me it didn't matter. His mannerism and the way he conducts comms is the absolute worst I've encountered through every instrument sim. He didn't ask anything in the brief. I got 2 5s, but he's still shitty.

C3401: He was great for aero. Has over 4,000 hours in a jet so he knows what he's talking about. He'll break away from the FTI procedures and make the maneuvers super simple. Just listen to him and do what he says and you'll hit air speeds and altitudes. Asked zero questions for the brief but just broke down the maneuvers.
C2202- doesnt care about anything except the PEL, know the PEL cold (I dont just mean what is in the briefing guide) know the procedures for the PEL cold and you'll crush it.

C2101 - Awesome guy. Leads the brief for you, so just know the hollywood script to the letter and you'll crush it. If you get through the checklist fast enough you'll have time to fly around which makes a good impression on him.

I2101 - SAY THIS :I WILL BE THE BEST INSTRUMENT PILOT. He also asks some cryptic questions during the brief, the answer is trim,scan and make corrections. Hes big on never accepting being off on alt, speed or heading. Take time to correct them and for the love of god do some opps checks during the sortie and remember your descen1wint checklist. He'll also likely throw the oil temp fail in the first few minutes, st people will miss it for the whole sim as theres no aural warning. Call it out and you'll get brownie points. Be humble and do your best when he beats you up but at the end he focuses on constructive and positive feedback. Graded much higher than I felt he would.

USMC jet guy, I crushed the brief for C3101 with him then he was cool the whole time, walking me through things and started preparing me for C3102 with our leftover time. He may seem stern at first, but if you know your stuff you can relax around him.
Tough and gives great tips throughout. Know your stuff and he'll spend st of the time trying to get you to understand the intricacies of the flightline and what to expect. Fair grader.

"Aim small, miss small." I took all his advice for my BI's and received 5's on st of my procedures for the next two BI's.. Best instructor so far. He will make you work. He asked me to brief all the procedures before the flight.
Super awesome guy, one of the best instructors I've bad yet. Chaplain to the pensacola minor league hockey team. Alst done writing a book.

Not bad if you know your stuff. Can be slightly hard on you but gave good grades. He will catch everything you do wrong and he may come off as nitpicky but don't let it get to you. Be honest about me weaknesses
. Make sure you know your procedures COLD. But objectively, he's a very vocal, honest person

Extremely particular and will correct you on everything. Talks really fast through everything so it's hard to get a word in during the brief and be able to show him that you studied, but doesn't grade as harshly as expected

He definitely picked apart everything for me too. He throws around the "Attention to detail" and "going through the tions" phrases a lot; making you think you're doing terribly. But he ended up grading me fairly.
Not as bad as I thought it would be. He said my brief was poor even though I answered the majority of his questions correctly. He yells in the sim too, but I just ignored it. (I3200 block)
Very nit picky and doesn't let any details slide. However, he's a nice guy and as long as you don't take what he says personally and just learn, he's a good instructor and grades very fairly.

C2101: Great instructor. Strict, but that's what you want out of your early instructors. Know the Hollywood checklist verbatim, and expect questions from the fine print inside the hollywood checklist. He will expect you to answer his questions immediately, or else he will simply move on. Overall great instructor, and I hope I get him again.

Quite surprised, was expecting far worse. I2200 block, critical but never yelled, allowed me to make mistakes and then paused and we talked then corrected them. I made the same mistakes many times and he never lost patience.

I2201. Wasn't as bad as I remembered from the first PEL sim where I got him literally jumping up and down yelling haha. Long brief where he consistently drilled the 6Ts and always know course vs radial vs heading. If you know everything for the brief he was relatively relaxed in the sim. Bring a copy of the SAT airport diagram and have a printout of IFR sectional. He will have you make all of the radio calls on the ground/in the air and monitor the NAVAID morse code. He will also have you try the maneuvers without the CDI, but I think most instructors do this too

I've had him C2101, C2102, and I2103. If you want to "get good", pray you have him. When you have him there are ZERO deviations from procedure. No additional words, no missing words, no similar words…nothing. Make sure you know your stuff and practice. It can seem very frustrating when he demands such attention to detail, but you come out of it better. If you have him in any part of the I2100 block, DO NOT DATA DUMP YOUR PREVIOUS PROCEDURES. We got into the sim for I2103 (Approach pattern and Unusual attitudes) and before we started the main topics for the day I did airspeed changes, both timed turns (half standard rate and standard rate), a steep turn, and an S-1 pattern. We then did the topics laid out for the day and he had me do a GCA.
He's really nice, but also some of the highest expectations of the instructors so far.
Very friendly and good natured. Ran the brief entirely but it was C2101 so may not be truly representative of his style. Enjoyed jokes and wasn't overly troubled with me ving slowly.
Definitely ask questions in the brief to show him you've read and thought about procedures, etc. He's pretty strict in the sim but he gives you good grades if you know your stuff.
Nice guy. He runs the brief himself and asks you questions on specifics throughout. If you know your discuss items and procedures he's not too bad in the sim.
One of my favorites. Funny guy and has fair expectations. Walks you through the sim; an overall good instructor

Pretty chill during the brief and spent a good bit complaining about the air force being the reason our checklists require mery. But then in the sim was picky about being verbatim and turned the heat on a little more than the brief would suggest. Debrief was chill and ended up grading a lot better than I thought.

I3205: Really really chill guy, will let you use the FMS to the best extent possible, even on events like this one where it says to use it only for GPS approaches. Easy to talk to and doesn't say a whole lot during the sim which is helpful for instrument sims where you can focus better. Likes to talk about flyin g, football and any other sports.

Very fun to sim with and very talkative. At the start of the brief be ready to rapid fire any EPs, discussion items as soon as the brief starts. If you can answer some brief questions for the next sim as well you will be on his good side. Don't let his casual attitude keep you from acting professionally. You may have to talk over his side comments to stay on topic/hit your marks/make radio calls, but he seemed to appreciate that I was focused. A really fun sim overall. He showed me some cool things and let me practice some parts of the next sim.

I2102 - Overall, he was super tivated. He showed me his way of scanning the instruments which was fine. Brief was very informaI. I didn't do so hot on the material during the flight and he gave me a 3's on the gradcard, so I'd say he was generous to say the least. Gradecard called to start at 12,00 MSL but he started me on the ground and was rushed to takeoff, not being able to set up any of my screens or switches, so I was behind the power curve all event. He was definitely patient and coached me through the maneuvers. He has much re of a "in your face" approach to instructing, so be ready for that. Debrief was probably the best one I've had. He printed out the route and we debriefed every single maneuver.

C2102: He was very systems-focused in regards to the high IOAT start. Specifically, brush up on what the PMU is going through during that checklist, and also, this seemed a bit random, but how IOAT is calculated. Also, know that the reason external power is better is because it provides re amps than a battery could. I went into this being familiar with this information so the rest of the sim went real well. Overall, he is a very nice guy, patient, and technically proficient.

Had him for I2203. SUPER nice guy but VERY talkative--I think he talked a lot during the sim to try and distra ct me to be honest. Otherwise If you know your stuff he grades well. Prior enlisted submariner.

Super nice. He speaks quietly so get ready to have to listen up. He does his research. We had an in depth convo about GPS systems from the 70s when subs had them before anyone else knew they existed, OBOGS and how traditional systems worked. Fair in the plane, gave me some techniques on how to sten radio calls. Not sure how he graded me, he never really said specifically. Went briefly over my next sim event. Overall positive guy, no helmet fire or uncomfortable pressure. Gives constructive helpful criticism that doesn't make you feel like crap.
C2201. Extremely nice, he is quiet as previously stated, and he looooooves to talk. I think we got to the sim about 40 minutes after a brief time. He was helpful, and taught me some good techniques.

C3401: Loves to talk. Speaks very, very softly so you have to strain to hear what he's saying. Didn't even talk about briefing items but went on tangents talking about his flying career for 45 minutes. Not the best communicator or instructor in the sim but not the worst. He didn't mess with me or anything in the flight until the end for power loss so we could do the SSR. Really nice guy and passionate about flying.

I2102: Definitely soft spoken, just lean in and try to relate. He is/was an engineer and really is passionate about the systems but not in a NATOPS way but rather a design and engineering way. Talked about how the PCL encodes your setting into binary and then works with the PMU and FMU, brought up how the AF fucked up the PT-6 by taking away features etc.Nearly a 50 minute "brief" in which I only answered 3 questions. Easy going in the sim, didn't seem to get on me much about not being perfect, graded higher than I expected.
Awesome guy. Very relaxed and helpful. Easy to talk to. Know your stuff coming in cause he will ask questions on discuss items but probably the best instructor I've had

C3102, last minute instructor change and I'm glad for it. Was Amazingly relaxed and helpful guy. Air Force retired IP who knows how to help you along with putting together the pattern. Focused on max 2 things to improve ever pass and wasn't overbearing pointing out corrections. Graded fair but not giving anything for free.
C2103: Very relaxed mannerisms. Doesn't freak out if you give a wrong number or answer. Fair grader (4s and 3s).

C3401: nice guy, asks lots of questions, doesn't care if you get them wrong, keeps on trucking along. Very involved mentoring in the SIM, fair grader. Very detailed comments, too detailed... with every mistake you made.
Super nice guy and a santa claus with the grades.

I2101: Wouldn't exactly call him a santa claus but if you know your stuff he grades well. Same with the brief, would probably be generous if you missed a few questions but he definitely took notice if you kill the brief. Nice guy, calm mannerisms and also talks just the right aunt for instrument stuff so you learn but can still make mistakes in order to I'll learn. Also he is not distracting which is great for instrument stuff.

I2103- USMC C-130 pilot, can be slightly intense but great to have a conversation with. Ask him questions and he'll help you wrap your head around topics without overcomplicating it. VT-3 reservist that has beat cancer and been on combat deployments. Very nice guy and helpful tips on maneuvers, nothing to be worried about here as long as you are prepared. Will make you do all maneuvers on the grade sheet.

I2101- Extremely nice guy who takes the time to get to know you a little bit before the hop. Flew E-6's, very informational about the material and lots of good tips to handle the aircraft. Easy going inside the aircraft, will let you make a mistake and correct without saying anything, but wants to see you recognize deviations. Come prepared to the brief and flight with the required knowledge and he will grade fairly.

FAM3101: Great instructor. 10/10. Got asked some questions about the pressurization system control valve and climb/cruise PCL settings at critical altitude. Great conversations about those, the discuss items, as well as other random topics pertaining to the FTI. Hop was smooth. Definitely wants to see you succeed.

Laid back and to the point. Has a farm with lots of animals, likes the outdoors, and did missions with Spec Ops. I knew the maneuvers very well going into the plane but lacked practice time so he helped coach me to really improve, especially on the S1 and timing/reading the clock. Graded me better than I thought. And gave me stretch/eye breaks every so often during the sim
For 12103: It was hard. He gets in the weeds with questions and is overly meticulous on dumb stuff (like which clock, Zulu or local, to count seconds). Fair grader.
I2103: sometimes you feel like you're terrible, but it's just because he's trying to point out habits and ways you can improve your scans. Very helpful albeit blunt.. fair grader.
Set in his ways. Harder grader than st. Inpatient, and yells.

Had him for my first sim. He had me do every single radio call, conduct the break, and was suppppper picky about the checklist. If you know your on stuff though he will be fine, graded me pretty fair.

C2101: went through the entire Hollywood checklist, went through radio calls in the checklists, very picky about being "verbatim", prefers you to have the checklist on left leg and blank paper on right leg for notes/writing down atis and clearances, fair grader but felt like I was not doing well during the sim
C2201. He talked for st of the brief. I got the 4 or 5 questions he asked right

though so that set a good tone for the rest of the sim. Very nitpicky on the hollywood checklist. I felt like I performed the EPs poorly, as he is very critical and quick to point out everything. Despite this, he gave me a good debrief and good grades. Toughest instructor I've had so far but also felt like I learned the st during this sim.

Honestly not nearly as bad as people make him out to be (maybe I caught him on a good day?) Anyway, the key with him is being prepared with intelligent questions at the beginning of the brief and showing up knowing your stuff. I had him for I2102 and he was pretty chill whenever I screwed something up; just recognize your mistake and correct it. Grades fairly.

For I2104, agreed with above. He isn't bad at all really. He grades fairly (doesn't give you brownie points but better than you think you did) and gives good advice. As always, the more prepared you are, the cooler the instructor will be, Tormey is no exception. When he gets nitpicky about your altitude or airspeed or heading, he isn't being a dick, he's trying to challenge you and it helps alot.
C2102: Goes deeper into NATOPS than st. Pulls questions directly from briefing guide. Very picky as stated above, but overall fair grader. You will feel like you're jacked up st of the time though.
One of the worst you can get. Gets way too far into the weeds to the point where you lose the whole point of the brief.

I33XX sim. Briefed for a whole hour and alst didn't have enough time to meet the training objectives for the event. Nice enough guy, 200IQ. Makes you feel like an idiot sometimes but it's only to prove whatever point he's getting at. My biggest takeaway from the sim was that he writes upside down really well.

He does indeed write upside down well. He was average level of difficulty during brief. Asked a lot of questions, but they were all fair game in brief guide and pretty easy. During the Sim he will be very strict with airspeed and altitude. I'm talking like 1 kg and 20ft. Honestly made me feel behind the aircraft to the point that I messed up a maneuver. After messing up, I thought I deserved a few threes, but even after a honest debrief, he still gave all 4s. He wants you to be perfect, but doesnt expect you to be perfect. Just relax, he's not too bad.

I2103: Pretty chill brief and sim. He talked for a solid 20 minutes on how flying should be like making music and about penmanship… Definitely particular on being off altitude and airspeed, and is quick to point it out. Don't take it the wrong way. One of the better sims I've had.

C2101: He is way more chill than these reviews make him out to be. He is by the book. You need to say EXACTLY what is in the hollywood script or he will correct you. Expected you to know everything you were supposed to (Checklists, radio calls) and then added a little extra by pulling the cockpit pressure circuit breaker to make sure I was paying attention during the ops check. Didn't add that to the grading however, just pushed a little further to get me thinking. Calm, quiet, fair grader. Know your stuff like you're supposed to and you'll be fine.

C2101: He is fine, not very personable and straight to the point. In our brief we didn't talk about the briefing guide at all, he just showed me a couple things about the ejection seat and asked me one question about the shear pin that I didn't know. Anyways, he didn't pull any new tricks aside from pulling the "Inflow SYS" circuit breaker once I was above 10,000 feet so he expected me to notice the cockpit altitude over 8,000 feet, which I did. Look out for that. Otherwise, its straight up checklist with radio calls. He also walked me through a entry/exit to NA and a return to homefield with course rules, to include radio calls, as well as the break.

I2203: Really nice old dude. Flew P-3s, so he's super particular about things, i.e. know the FTI procedures for whatever you're doing. Gave good tips/tricks, and also went into a lot of detail to make sure you understood the concepts being taught.
Will know if you just copied the jet logs/DD-175's for the later instrument sims

I3101: Asked literally everything in the briefing guide that was 50 pages long. Couldn't get a break, i guess he was being too tough. If you were not verbatim on comms, and didn't magically know how he wanted the approach plates briefed, he oversaturated you with his techniques. Would not give any tips for the next sim other than "be prepared like you are today". Thanks a lot. :
He's rible. Will try to trip you up. Gave me an unsat. Just imsafe out of it

He's not a bad guy, I have a feeling some of the people above weren't very prepared. He does ask a lot of questions to make sure you know what you're doing, and will freeze the sim to ask you a question too, but he's very even toned and didn't get frustrated with me at all. Honestly he gave really good instruction and I learned a lot from him. had him for I2202.

Came in very prepared and he graded fairly, but was hands down the st miserable experience in sim-land by a long shot. Would constantly interrupt you and freeze the sim. For BI he also made me go off the 27 instead of the 57 and do the GCA with left turns. Seemed to enjoy making things more difficult than they needed to be for no apparent reason and trying to trip you up.

I3204: This guy gets a bad rap for some reason. He wasn't a push over, but gave good grades, and brief wasn't complicated. I'm not sure what you'd have to do to unsat with him. He helped out in the sim too. He failed the cockpit pressurization for me to notice in my climb, and he failed my DME, but he still wasn't even close to the worst.

I3203: I don't believe this guy merits being called one of the 4 semen. He isn't that bad. He will definitely try and teach you his techniques specifically, which you might not be entirely ready for but just go along with it. He is tough in the brief, but you're not going to get yelled at for getting anything wrong. Go in with a good attitude, he is an instructor who genuinely just wants you to learn.

Agreed ^ had him for I2103, and he was one of the better instructors I've had. The questions he asked were pretty standard, and as long as you know the FTI items the brief should be tough but simple. He gives you good opportunities to show what you know, and isn't rude or aggressive about correcting the things you don't. During the sim he would pause after the maneuvers to discuss what you did well and what you need to work on. If you show up well prepared and with a good attitude, he'll be a really great instructor and grade more than fairly.

FAM3101: He's a nice guy and wants you to come prepared like you've really read the procedures, but he also will teach you a lot. He starts out letting you recite the procedures but if he can tell you know them he takes over and teaches more. If you mess up he's understanding and will correct you as long as you learn from your mistake he moves on quickly. Overall really nice guy has a lot of good info to teach and tells you exactly what he expects from the start.

C2102:. if you go in with a tough knowledge of everything on the briefing guide he is awesome. He puts a big emphasis on knowing your stuff in the brief and then gave me some slack during the sim for minor mistakes. He asked me about the battery voltages for when to connect external power and what to keep in mind about ejecting on the ground (if you are under the parking tent, you will hit the roof). If you ask questions and interact while he is talking he will help you out. I learned a lot from him. We wrapped up most of C2102 with a few minutes to spare so he showed me what to expect for C2103

He's awesome. Had him for C3101 and if you know your procedures cold in the brief, he is very generous with the airwork. He gives great advice and also prepped me for the next sim. He swears a lot and he can get loud but its not him getting mad, he's just trying to get through your helmet fire if you have one (pattern work for me). Get him talking, laugh at his jokes and you'll be on his good side from the start. If you come prepared with a question (doesn't necessarily have to be about that brief's discussion items), you'll be off to a good start because it shows you're trying to learn.
C3401: Great guy to have a sim with overall. He explains things in a way that helps you understand and wants you to do well. Show up with your job done by studying and he will teach you a lot!
Have had three sims with him now. One of my favorite instructors!

Nice guy and fair grader but definitely tells it like it is during sim and debrief (not a bad thing but if you made mistakes be prepared). For basic instrument sims is big on having the instrument scan table merized (at least top 3 rows)

Former USMC CH-46 pilot, calm and patient personality, wry sense of hur. Brief went slightly outside the scope of the briefing guide, expects that you know your gear for contacts sims. Don't let him trick you into missing checklist items, fair grader and nice guy overall.

I2104. Great instructor, very calm. He let me make my mistakes, recognize them, and then fix them. A quick question he likes to ask for this event: Q. What instruments are left after a dual IAC failure? A. BFI, Standby VHF, and Clock. They all run off of the Aux Bat and will last for a max of 30 minutes.
really good, suggested putting your PCL under your knee board to help prop up your forearm
Extremely helpful. Will focus on necessary items for the sim but will go above and beyond in helping you understand basic airwork and what will be expected of you in the plane
Really cool, I had him for C2102 and he talked alot about his techniques for where to put stuff in the cockpit, strap-in, and hanging the mask from your vest

He is definitely the man. For instruments he will make you do the same thing he did in contacts- have all your pubs and be prepared to have that crap in the 2200 sims all in your way. Super good about giving you his teq though.
C2102 Awesome instuctor. Know your stuff and he will fill in the gaps/give you more than you could ask. Learned a lot.

Had him for C2102. Likes to talk, enjoys teaching. Nice guy. Gave me my fire light during my engine shutdown at the same time that I turned avionics switch off when other cautions go off so it was hard to catch. Said he does that to everyone. Times you how fast you can get out during fire o the ground.
I had him for my first sim. Very approachable and eager to help with mistakes. Grades fairly.
